scope: NCollection_Buffer initialized raw-policy constructor adoption and adjacent safe incremental owned-byte lease race correction
integration_status: Candidate; root merge/check/deletion and full integrated checkpoint required.
source_scope: Buffer, allocator implementation, selected tests and new/prior native probes archived; not the full compiler/dependency closure.

method_bindings.domain: Non-null allocator handle; null pointer follows normal allocation; non-null exact raw-policy allocation with initialized exclusive prefix size <= allocation extent and isize::MAX.

constructor_behavior: Previously only AllocatedBytes owners could enter Buffer; the new unsafe constructor transfers a live allocate_raw/allocate_optimal_raw allocation directly without allocating, freeing, copying or zeroing its contents.

The selected non-null allocator and actual freeing owner are the same identity. Logical prefix size remains independent of full raw allocation size; heap headers retain the complete allocation layout for release.
Null data delegates to Buffer::new: all normal/null/zero allocation behavior remains, including accumulating Free(nullptr) Standard_ProgramError and invalid aligned allocation returning empty.

Incremental adoption registers one owned-byte lease before safe slices can escape. Reset is denied until that owner is released; two adopted allocations retain independent leases, zero-sized adoption also pins the arena, and allocator replacement releases the old lease.

All five policies preserve prefix contents, pointer identity and endpoints through raw/optimal adoption. Native accumulating allocation count stays 1 during adoption and drops to 0 after destruction; incremental cursor advances only by the original raw request.
The existing with_data and with_data_size adapters retain their behavior and safe original-owner release semantics.

existing_allocator_defect.description: Safe BaseAllocator::allocate previously called allocate_policy, released the Incremental mutex, then reacquired it to increment live ownership. Concurrent safe reset(true) could free the block before the allocation was zeroed or returned.
existing_allocator_defect.correction: allocate_owned_address now holds one engine guard across Incremental allocate(size) and acquire(), before exposing or zeroing the address. Other policies retain their prior allocation route. allocate_typed was inspected and already holds its guard across allocate_aligned and acquire; it was unchanged.
existing_allocator_defect.baseline_kind: Controlled reconstruction of the old split-window ordering within the candidate, not a claim that the entire untouched main revision was run. Only allocate_owned_address was replaced with allocate_policy followed by separately locked acquire_owned_byte_lease; new API/tests remained available.
existing_allocator_defect.baseline_result: Miri reports dangling access in owned.rs zeroing after another thread deallocates through reset/raw_heap.
existing_allocator_defect.proof_scope: The captured seed reproduces the defect and passes after correction. The structural single-lock proof excludes the split window; a barrier-controlled test separately proves a returned allocation blocks another thread reset until drop. Neither stress tests nor one seed claim exhaustive schedule exploration.

native_scenarios: Five policies x Allocate/AllocateOptimal x logical prefix sizes0,1,4,16; null-pointer sizes0,4; allocator replacement and reallocation for all policies; explicit Free and raw zero allocation for non-accumulating policies; accumulating live counts and incremental cursor.
remaining_gaps: The unsafe constructor requires initialized bytes, exclusive ownership, original raw-policy provenance and allocation validity until adoption returns. Typed allocator-api2/AllocBox/AllocVec and foreign C heap pointers are explicitly rejected by contract; no broad arbitrary raw pointer compatibility is claimed.

Null-selected allocator leaks, native arbitrary allocator subclass callbacks, uninitialized byte exposure, throw-time requested-size observation and destructor exception/termination behavior remain outside the adapter.

Accumulating zero-byte raw allocation at a block end can be rejected by native Free; that pre-existing edge and repeated Free(nullptr) destructor failure are not silently declared equivalent to Rust Drop. Zero logical prefix over a valid nonzero raw allocation is tested for all policies.
Native matrix is x86_64 Linux. Generic platform ABI or complete Buffer/allocator class equivalence is not established.
Global API inventory and legacy declaration status remain unchanged; the one constructor-domain binding is a scoped candidate, not new full-class coverage.
validation_history: Native Heap handle required explicit base handle construction for the probe. Exploratory normal checks passed before controlled baseline reconstruction; final normal/Miri/docs/Clippy/fmt were rerun after restoring the final corrected source. No source mutation occurred during final checks.
